ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — MOCK EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. run
   C. happiness
   D. quickly

2. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. No full stops
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

3. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. Where is the library
   C. Where is the Library
   D. where is the library

4. When practising Pre Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pre Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pre Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Pre Reading.

5. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

6. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only a joining word

7. When practising Attentive listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Attentive listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Attentive listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive listening.

8. When practising Phonics, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Phonics.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Phonics.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Phonics.

9. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.

10. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.

11. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

12. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goed
   C. goes
   D. going

13. When practising Language School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Language School.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Language School.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Language School.

14. When practising Language Welcome and, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Language Welcome and.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Language Welcome and.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Language Welcome and.

15. When practising Pre-Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-Writing.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pre-Writing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Pre-Writing.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Connected text and fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Pre-Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Handwriting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Attentive listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Language Welcome and and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
